title: Gap width, wavelength and diffraction experiments practice

evidence_basis.evidence_gap_note: No primary-mapped P2 leaf currently covers this outcome; no P1 lesson assignment inferred.

questions.prompt: The wavelength of water waves is fixed. Which gap produces the most marked diffraction?

options.A: A gap much wider than the wavelength
options.B: A gap about equal to the wavelength
options.C: A gap ten times the wavelength
options.D: All gap widths produce equal spreading

questions.prompt: One gap is used for two sets of waves. Which set spreads more after the gap?

options.A: The set with the longer wavelength
options.B: The set with the shorter wavelength
options.C: Both sets spread equally because the gap is unchanged
options.D: Neither set can diffract through a gap

questions.prompt: In a ripple-tank test of the effect of gap width, which choice makes the comparison fair?

options.A: Change gap width and frequency together
options.B: Change water depth for every gap
options.C: Keep wavelength fixed and change only gap width
options.D: Keep gap width fixed and change only wavelength

figure.purpose: Assess comparison of diffraction for two gap-width-to-wavelength relationships.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white two-panel ripple-tank diagram. Equal incoming wavefront spacing approaches gap P about one wavelength wide and gap Q about four wavelengths wide. Show no outgoing wavefronts; provide blank regions for the learner to predict.
figure.alt_text: Equal-wavelength waves approach a narrow gap P and a wider gap Q.

parts.prompt: State which gap gives the more strongly curved emerging wavefronts.
Explain your choice by comparing gap width with wavelength.
State one observation, other than curvature, that would indicate stronger diffraction.
Describe how to use a ripple tank to investigate how diffraction depends on gap width while wavelength stays fixed.
State the expected change in the outgoing wavefronts as the gap is reduced from many wavelengths wide to about one wavelength wide.

figure.purpose: Mix prior diffraction recognition with current relative-scale reasoning.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white plan view of one doorway. Panel X shows widely spaced sound wavefronts; panel Y shows closely spaced shorter-wavelength wavefronts. The doorway width is identical and a listener is placed around the corner.
figure.alt_text: Long- and short-wavelength waves meet the same doorway with a listener around the corner.

parts.prompt: Name the behaviour that allows waves to reach the listener around the doorway edge.
Predict which panel shows more spreading and explain your answer.
Explain why the statement 'only the longer-wavelength waves diffract' is incorrect.
